remaining_specs.title: Solve independent events from any sufficient pair

implementation.contract: Exactly two distinct constraints. Independence is explicit. Return all valid labeled solutions, an underdetermined state, or a clear inconsistent-input error.
implementation.normalize: Turn notA into known p=1−notA, and notB into known q=1−notB. Swap A/B consistently when only q is known.

aggregate_equations.U,N: U+N=1 is redundant; U=0 uniquely forces p=q=0, otherwise generally underdetermined

implementation.root_solver: When S=p+q and J are known: discriminant=S²−4J. Stable large=(S+sqrt(discriminant))/2 and small=J/large (or both zero if large=0). Return both label assignments unless equal.
validation: Inputs in [0,1]. Check every candidate against original constraints and all forward probabilities. Reject materially negative discriminants and probabilities outside [0,1]. Clamp only roundoff with a documented epsilon-scaled tolerance.
Zero divisor with zero residual means underdetermined; nonzero residual means inconsistent. Do not divide before this classification.
Use stable product-root recovery to retain tiny probabilities. Avoid setting all residuals below a broad absolute 1e−8 threshold to zero.

remaining_specs.title: Repeated independent trials and joint groups

formula: Cross-group events multiply the appropriate independent group probabilities.
implementation.stability: Use exp(n*log1p(−p)) for none and −expm1(n*log1p(−p)) for at least one. Handle p=0 and p=1 before logs. Repeat counts must be safe integers; do not loop per trial.
implementation.suggested_limit: n <= Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER or a documented smaller bound; no need to generate simulated trials.

remaining_specs.title: Infinite normal bounds and central-coverage table

implementation.input_change: Use explicit finite/negative-infinity/positive-infinity selectors, or a narrow bound parser accepting only finite numeric grammar, -inf, inf, +inf. Keep ordinary number fields finite.
formula: For standardized bounds zl,zu: probability = Φ(zu)−Φ(zl). Use SF(zl)−SF(zu) on positive tails. Φ(−∞)=0; Φ(+∞)=1.
Outside interval = probability below lower + probability above upper.
Central coverage C uses z=SF inverse((1−C)/2); displayed interval is [mean−z*sd, mean+z*sd].
implementation.table: Competitor shows central normal coverage intervals. Label them as central coverage/prediction bounds, not a confidence interval for an estimated mean: the input has no sample size.
validation: sd > 0; lower <= upper. Infinities only occur as intentional bounds and may be represented as strings in outputs.
Do not copy the competitor 68.28% label for exactly ±1 sd; correct normal coverage is approximately 68.2689492137%.

remaining_specs.title: Large integers, decimal places, unique decimals and sort

implementation.proposed_mode: Replace or extend the current random mode; do not keep Number parsing for exact bounds.
implementation.integer_algorithm: R=max−min+1 as BigInt. If R=1 return min. Otherwise k=bit length(R−1). Draw ceil(k/8) random bytes, mask unused high bits, interpret unsigned integer x, reject x>=R, return min+x. Never use Number conversion for bounds/range/results.
implementation.decimal_algorithm: Choose a fixed grid of step 10^(−d). Convert exact decimal lower/upper to grid indices L=ceil(lower*10^d), U=floor(upper*10^d). Sample integer j in [L,U], then format j/10^d with d decimal places. Reject an empty grid.
implementation.endpoint_contract: Suggested new contract: inclusive bounds for both integer and grid modes. The existing decimal mode declares [min,max); if retaining that contract use U=ceil(max*10^d)−1 instead. Document the chosen policy; observations do not prove endpoint probabilities.
implementation.unique_algorithm: Sample grid indices without replacement, using Floyd sampling or a sparse partial Fisher–Yates map. Check count <= U−L+1 first. Avoid rejection loops that become impractical near a full population.
implementation.sorting: Compare exact BigInts/grid indices; never lexicographically sort numeric strings or convert huge values to Number.
implementation.limits: Use explicit digit, decimal-place, count, and total rendered-character limits. Competitor advertises up to 999 decimal digits and a few thousand integer digits. Supporting a smaller bound is an intentional documented limitation, not full parity.
implementation.evidence_precision: Five bounded requests confirm precision=2 means two decimal places for 10–20 and 1000–2000; precision=4 gives four. Decimal + no duplicates + ascending is accepted and returns sorted distinct values.
implementation.non_goal: No claim that test fixtures predict real draws. Inject a byte source only in test harness; production uses crypto.getRandomValues.

fixtures.expected_error: Only two grid values are available.
The requested precision leaves no values inside the range.

remaining_specs.title: Radians and bounded pi input for angle fields

implementation.input_change: Add degree/radian selection only to angular fields or modes. For right-triangle pair mode, convert only first/second quantities whose selected key is A or B; lengths and areas stay unchanged.
implementation.parser: A bounded numeric literal or a simple coefficient times pi divided by a nonzero numeric literal is sufficient (pi, -pi/6, 2*pi/3, 0.5*pi). No arbitrary JS evaluation, identifiers, nested calls or assignment.
implementation.conversion: degrees = radians * 180 / pi. Reuse existing solver domain restrictions after conversion. Sector area K=r²*theta/2 in radians.
implementation.validation: Respect the explicit supported SSA angular range; show those bounds consistently in degrees/radians.

remaining_specs.title: Independent dimension units and dimensional output conversion

implementation.fields: Each length dimension has its own unit selector. Add an output area/volume unit selector. Convert all dimensions to one canonical unit before evaluating the existing shape formula.
implementation.formula: Area output = areaInM2/(outputLengthFactor²); volume output = volumeInM3/(outputLengthFactor³). If selecting litre/gallon, use a dedicated volume factor, not a length factor.
validation: All lengths use length units, while computed area/volume has the appropriate power.
Normalize units in calculation inputs without changing user-entered displayed values.

implementation.log: Permit the single constant e wherever the log form accepts a base/argument; translate to Math.E or high-precision e as appropriate, with existing log domain validation.
implementation.scientific: Permit a narrowly validated coefficient × 10^integerExponent form in both converter and arithmetic inputs, in addition to e notation. Normalize x, × or * only in this exact pattern. Do not evaluate arbitrary expressions.
implementation.validation: Bound length and exponent; preserve zero, negative coefficient and signed exponent. Reject trailing instructions or second expressions.

remaining_specs.title: Bring margin inverse confidence range in line with audited form

implementation.input_change: Raise confidence maximum from 99.99 to 99.999, matching existing sample-size mode and audited form.
implementation.formula: e = inverseNormalSf((1−C)/2) * sqrt(p(1−p)/n) * FPC; use direct upper tail to avoid cancellation.
implementation.census: For finite N=n, return zero sampling margin; N=n=1 is a census and must not use FPC=1. Alternatively reject N=1 with a clear unsupported-population explanation, rather than return a wrong positive value.

formulas: With opposite-side labels fixed: A=(0,0); B=(c,0); C=(x,y), x=(b²+c²−a²)/(2c), y=2K/c.
implementation.numeric_policy: Use normalized dimensions to avoid intermediate overflow. For nearly degenerate triangles, disclose unsupported precision rather than emitting wildly large/infinite centers.
implementation.steps: Show a short calculated substitution for the selected solution method; do not copy competitor prose.

remaining_specs.title: DMS coordinate input

implementation.input_change: Offer DMS + hemisphere alongside decimal degree inputs; convert into the existing great-circle routine.
implementation.formula: decimal = hemisphereSign * (degrees + minutes/60 + seconds/3600). N/E positive; S/W negative. Degrees are a nonnegative magnitude when a hemisphere is selected.
validation: Minutes and seconds in [0,60). Latitude at most 90°, longitude at most 180°. If degree value is at its maximum, minutes and seconds must be zero.
Do not silently combine a negative degree sign with a conflicting hemisphere.

implementation.formula: For finite slope m: intercept=y1−m*x1, line y=m*x+intercept; inclination=atan(m) with a documented undirected [0,180°) or signed convention. Vertical line x=x1, inclination 90°.
implementation.current: Two-point mode reports slope/intercept/distance; only the vertical case has an equation string. Endpoint mode returns points only.
